decisions.rationale: 'familial breast cancer' names one disease concept (breast cancer with a familial pattern) and is not a family of multiple specific diseases, so it is a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease vs Disease Class)

decisions.rationale: 'breast cancer' is used as a noun modifier of 'families' in 'breast cancer families', so it is a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: 'breast / ovarian cancer' is a contiguous string referring to two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer), so it is a Composite Mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 2 (Contiguous text strings / Composite Mention)

decisions.rationale: 'breast cancer' modifies 'families' in 'Dutch breast cancer families', so it is a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: 'ovarian cancer' appears as a head noun ('one case of ovarian cancer') and refers to one specific disease, so it is a Specific Disease.
'breast and / or ovarian cancer' is a contiguous string covering two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer), so it is a Composite Mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 2 (Contiguous text strings / Composite Mention)

decisions.rationale: 'breast-ovarian cancer' is a contiguous hyphenated string referring to two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer), so it is a Composite Mention even though it modifies 'families'.
